newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH LEADER GETS PNUEMONIA AFTER CANCER SURGERY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH LEADER GETS PNUEMONIA AFTER CANCER SURGERY.

text.p: A Czech surgeon said on Thursday that President Vaclav Havel had developed pneumonia following surgery to remove a cancerous lung tumour earlier this week.

But Dr. Pavel Pavko told a news conference that tests showed there appears to be no spreading of the cancer after the radical surgery which removed a small malignant tumour along with half of Havel's right lung.
"The health condition of the president has gotten slightly complicated," Pavko said.
"A slight pneumonia is starting" in Havel's left lung, he added. "This is not very often a complication, but it sometimes happens."

Pavko said that tests showed that there was no "metastasis" after the surgery on Monday, meaning the cancer had not spread. He said a team of physicians, including cancer specialists, would meet again early next week to discuss Havel's progress.
Havel, aged 60 and a heavy smoker, entered hospital on November 25 after his office said he was suffering from a case of pneumonia.
